explanation:
[EFFECT]
Higher wind speed consistently reduces predicted bike demand, with the effect becoming stronger as wind picks up. At calm conditions (near 0 km/h), wind has little to no impact on the model's prediction, but as wind speed rises toward 30–40 km/h and beyond, the contribution turns increasingly negative, meaning the model predicts noticeably fewer rentals. The relationship is broadly monotonic — the faster the wind, the greater the drag on demand — with the most severe drops occurring at the highest recorded wind speeds (above ~45 km/h).

[IMPORTANCE]
Wind speed ranks 8th out of 9 features in overall importance (importance score ≈ 0.020), making it one of the weakest drivers of predicted demand in this model. Its influence is real but modest compared to factors like hour of day, temperature, or weather situation.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Because high winds meaningfully suppress demand but are a relatively minor factor overall, operations teams should focus wind-related adjustments mainly on unusual high-wind events (roughly above 30–40 km/h), where reducing bike availability or deferring rebalancing runs could save unnecessary effort on days when riders are unlikely to show up.
